title: Activation Functions: A Reading Guide
description: Nine focused guides to activation values, gradients, numerical stability, SwiGLU, and designing a function of your own.

title: Why Neural Networks Need Activation Functions
description: See where an activation sits, why linear layers collapse, and how its slope affects learning.

title: Sigmoid and Tanh: Bounded Outputs and Saturation
description: Understand bounded activations, derive their slopes, and separate hidden-layer saturation from probability outputs.

title: Stable Sigmoid: Avoiding Overflow in Exponentials, Log-Sigmoid, and Losses
description: Prevent exponential overflow with the two-branch sigmoid identity, preserve tail precision in log-sigmoid, and derive stable binary cross-entropy from logits.

title: ReLU, Leaky ReLU, and PReLU: What Happens Below Zero?
description: Follow ReLU through its gradient, then see how fixed and learned negative slopes change the behavior.

title: GELU and SELU: Gaussian Weighting and Self-Normalizing Scale
description: Unpack the Gaussian CDF and product-rule derivative for GELU, then compare ELU and SELU's exponential negative branch and self-normalizing conditions.

title: SiLU and Swish: Smooth Self-Gating
description: Explain sigmoid-weighted inputs, derive their slopes, and see how Swish scales the transition.

title: SwiGLU: One Learned Branch Controls Another
description: Build SwiGLU from SiLU, trace both branches and their gradients, and compare feed-forward blocks at equal parameter budgets.

title: Softmax: Turn Competing Scores into Probabilities
description: Explain vector-valued softmax, stable computation, its coupled derivatives, and the connection to cross-entropy.

title: How to Design an Activation Function
description: Build a smooth leaky activation from a desired slope, check its mathematics and numerics, and plan a fair training comparison.
